counterexample.initialized_ticks: 0 (liquidityNet +L), 100 (liquidityNet 0, liquidityGross 2L) and 200 (liquidityNet -L), from positions over [0, 100) and [100, 200), each with liquidity L
counterexample.note: Tick 100 is initialized but its liquidityNet is 0, so the patch calls _advanceToNextDown and skips it. The liquidity sum happens to match, but an initialized tick inside the walk is missing. The hook then never adds growth to rewardGrowthOutsideX128[100], so the reward earned between tick 100 and the start price goes to the [0, 100) position instead of the [100, 200) position.

summary: For an aligned start tick, reads the tick's liquidityNet from the pool and keeps the start tick only when liquidityNet is not zero. An initialized start tick whose liquidityNet is zero is still skipped.
